intervals.note: Mirrors the experiment:gerda Phase I interval (same source and quote).
intervals.quote: The first phase (Phase I), from November 2011 to May 2013, accumulated an exposure of 21.6 kg⋅yr with a background of about 10−2 cts/(keV⋅kg⋅yr) at Qββ

intervals.label: Phase II data taking
intervals.note: Phase II data set used for the final result. The official GERDA home page separately states that data taking stopped in February 2020 (see the completed interval).
intervals.quote: GERDA Phase II data were collected between December 2015 and November 2019.

intervals.label: completed
intervals.note: Official GERDA page: data taking stopped in February 2020; the LEGEND collaboration took over the setup.

name: GERDA detector
notes: Placed at site:lngs-hall-a (dangling reference: owned by the 'facilities' lead, not yet created).

placements.note: Start (2011-11) is the start of Phase I data taking (see intervals); end (2020-02) is when data taking stopped per the cited page; the quote supports the Hall A location and the end date, not the start. site:lngs-hall-a is owned by the facilities lead and may not exist yet in this repository (dangling reference, expected per ID_REGISTRY row 54).
placements.quote: The GERDA experiment searched for neutrinoless double-beta (0νββ) decay of 76Ge by operating Ge detectors made from 76Ge enriched material in a 64 m3 liquid argon cryostat located in Hall A of LNGS. Data taking stopped in Febr 2020.

isotope.quote: The GERDA experiment searched for neutrinoless double-beta (0νββ) decay of 76Ge

isotope_mass.locator: Max Planck Institute for Physics, GERDA page
isotope_mass.quote: GERDA also employed detectors made of germanium-76. ... the GERDA experiment utilized a total of 40 kilograms of detector material

summary.plain: Bare germanium crystals submerged directly in a huge tank of ultra-cold liquid argon, deep under an Italian mountain, listening for a rare kind of radioactive decay.
summary.technical: Array of bare, enriched (76Ge) high-purity germanium point-contact detectors (~40 kg total) submerged directly in a 64 m³ liquid-argon cryostat that serves as both cooling medium and active veto, in LNGS Hall A.

technology.quote: operating Ge detectors made from 76Ge enriched material in a 64 m3 liquid argon cryostat
technology.value: Bare enriched-germanium point-contact detectors immersed in a liquid-argon cryostat
